nodes.name: Chronopotentiometry Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: A graphite rod and Ag/AgCl (3.0 M KCl) used as the counter electrode and reference electrode, respectively, and the NiFe foam substrate as the working electrode used CHI 760e workstation for all tests. The Ce-NiFe catalyst was electrodeposited in an electrolyte containing Ni2+, Fe3+, and Ce3+ in nitrate solution. For amorphous Ce-NiFe, the total amount of Ni2+, Fe3+, and Ce3+ in the electrolyte were maintained at 0.1 M. The Ce3+ ion content was 10% of the total molar concentration. The amorphous Ce-NiFe was electrodeposited at 20 mA cm-2 for 500 s.

unit_operations.name: Electrodeposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the amorphous Ce-NiFe was electrodeposited for different times at 20 mA cm-2.

nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Amorphous Ce-NiFe: A graphite rod and Ag/AgCl ... the amorphous Ce-NiFe was electrodeposited for different times at 20 mA cm-2.

nodes.name: Cyclic Voltammetry Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The electrodeposition was conducted in an electrolyte containing Ce3+, Ni2+, and Fe3+. The total amount of Ni2+, Fe3+, and Ce3+ in the electrolyte were maintained at 0.1 M. The Ce3+ ion content was varied in the electrolyte with 10% of the total molar concentration. The potential window of CV was from 0.2 to -1.2 V versus Ag/AgCl. The scanning rate was controlled at 100 mV s-1 for ten cycles to get the nanocrystalline Ce-NiFe.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Nanocrystalline Ce-NiFe: The electrodeposition was conducted ... for ten cycles to get the nanocrystalline Ce-NiFe.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The NiFe foam (2.5 x 2 cm2) was immersed into a 75 mL Teflon autoclave vessel filled with a solution (63 mL) containing Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (3.88 mmol), Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (1.12 mmol), Ce(NO3)3·6H2O (0.56 mmol) (the molar ratio of Ni, Fe, and Ce was 7:2:1), NH4F (10 mmol), and CO(NH)2 (25 mmol) and heated to 120 °C for 8 h. After cooled down to room temperature, the crystalline Ce-NiFe supported on the NiFe foam was washed with pure water several times.

unit_operations.name: Washing

nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Crystalline Ce-NiFe: The NiFe foam (2.5 x 2 cm2) ... washed with pure water several times.

nodes.name: NiFe Control Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The electrodeposition of NiFe-based hydroxides was conducted in an electrolyte containing Ni2+ and Fe3+ by dissolving each chemical in pure water under sonication. The total concentration of Ni2+ and Fe3+ in the electrolyte were maintained at 0.1 M. The NiFe was electrodeposited on substrate at 20 mA cm-2 for 500 s.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of NiFe: The electrodeposition of NiFe-based hydroxides ... at 20 mAcm-2 for 500 s.

nodes.name: Substitution Synthesis (Eu-NiFe)
nodes.procedure: The Eu-NiFe catalyst was fabricated using the same electrodeposition approach as the amorphous Ce-NiFe, substituting Ce3+ with Eu3+ in the nitrate electrolyte solution at 20 mA cm-2 for 500 s.
nodes.source_text: We fabricated the f-block element-doped NiFe-based catalysts using the same electrodeposition approach with the amorphous Ce-NiFe.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals the nanoscale amorphous structure of the Ce-NiFe catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image (Figure 1b) further reveals the nanoscale amorphous Ce-NiFe catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms the amorphous nature of Ce-NiFe due to the absence of lattice stripes, while NiFe shows lattice spacings of 0.21 and 0.15 nm corresponding to Ni(OH)2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image shows that distinct lattice stripes were not observed in Ce-NiFe (Figure 1c), indicating the amorphous nature of the sample.

properties.observation: Shows a granular texture with no clear long-range atomic order or distinct lattice fringes, indicative of an amorphous or very fine nanocrystalline material.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED patterns of Ce-NiFe show no diffraction points, supporting the amorphous nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, no diffraction points of the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns were observed in inset of Figure 1c.

properties.observation: Displays a diffuse halo, characteristic of an amorphous or extremely fine nanocrystalline material, rather than sharp diffraction spots or rings of a well-crystallized material.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows only substrate peaks for Ce-NiFe and NiFe, confirming their amorphous or nanocrystalline structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic diffraction peaks of amorphous Ce-NiFe and NiFe exhibit only three diffraction peaks originated from the NiFe foam by X-ray diffraction (XRD) ... indicating that Ce-NiFe and the NiFe deposited onto NiFe substrates have amorphous or nanocrystalline structures

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra exhibit peaks at 460 and 525 cm-1 assigned to Ni-OH and Ni-O in the Ni(OH)2 phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2b, the two main peaks at 460 and 525 cm−1 are assigned to the Ni - OH and Ni - O in the Ni(OH)2.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms Ni2+, Fe3+, and mixed valence Ce3+/Ce4+. Doping with Ce induces positive binding energy shifts in Ni 2p, Fe 2p, and O 1s peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The details for the peak deconvolution of Ni2+ 2p3/2 (856.40 eV) in amorphous Ce-NiFe have a positive shift (0.24 eV) ... suggesting that the Fe ion in amorphous Ce-NiFe was transformed into high oxidation state by the high valent f-block element
